newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani Islamists demand Bhutto's ouster.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani Islamists demand Bhutto's ouster.

text.p: Pakistani Islamists on Friday accused Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government of corruption and demanded its dismissal, eyewitnesses said.
The demand was made at a rally attended by more then 20,000 supporters of the rightist Jamaat-i-Islami party in the industrial port city of Karachi, one witness said.
Protesters chanted slogans against Bhutto and accused her government of corruption during a five-mile (eight km) march which ended near Karachi's port.

"The government is corrupt. It has plundered the nation's wealth ... President Farooq Leghari should dismiss it," Jamaat's chief Qazi Hussain Ahmed told the rally outside the mausoleum of Pakistan's founder Mohammad Ali Jinnah.

The marchers, some of them wearing headbands with the slogan Allah-o-Akbar (God is great) were carrying hundreds of flags and placards inscribed with slogans against the government and vowed to resist what they called the negative influence of Western culture in Pakistan.
Eyewitnesses said youths damaged dozens of advertisement billboards showing women, while the cinemas on the route of the rally covered up posters of film actors and actresses.
Ahmed said his party aims to bring about an Islamic revolution in the country and will not allow the promotion of anti-Islamic culture.
He said corruption had passed all limits and the country had plunged into an economic crisis.
No government comment was immediately available.
Ahmed accused high government officials of conspiring in the murder of Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza.
"We want an accountability of the rulers... People are now fed up with the feudals. They want a clean government," he said.
